exact_claims.statement: For fixed ordinary degree limits and fixed path length, the patch construction in Lemma affine-patches gives uniformly bounded degrees and nonzero integer evaluated minors whose product has absolute value at most X^K for a fixed K, independent of z, all blocks and initial equation coefficients.

assessment: The actual projection, evaluation-nullspace and proper-intersection recursion supplies coefficient-free bounded-height patches. Bounded-size integer cofactors control equations independently of evaluation-row count; strict containment cuts to lower dimension, while equality gives a generically nonzero Jacobian minor and a lower-dimensional boundary. Reducibility, singularities and non-rational geometric components are covered by componentwise degree bounds and descent. Parent integration matched the necessary total-component degree convention to manuscript lines 20-24 and the weighted-box and initial-complexity hypotheses to lines 37-68; this is not a remaining source gap.
supported_scope: Finite integral S in the fixed weighted box, X >= 2, fixed ambient dimension and fixed bound on total geometric degree, with no initial coefficient or sample-cardinality bound.
Uniform component, equation and boundary degrees under kernel intersections, including failed dimension drops and retained components.
Descent of non-Q-defined geometric components and renewed descent after every component split.
Generic codimension-many low-degree equations obtained from same-dimensional coordinate projections in characteristic zero; no global complete-intersection hypothesis.
Integer bounded-height nullspace bases from cofactors, deterministic bounded normalization, and coverage of singular and zero-dimensional exceptional pieces.
For fixed ordinary degree limits and fixed path length, a uniform nonzero integer minor product bounded in absolute value by X^K.
At most floor(K/zeta) distinct divisors from primes at least X^zeta, without independence of the product from the prime choices.
unresolved_obligations: The source degree convention and initial theorem hypotheses have been matched to manuscript lines 20-24 and 37-68. The cumulative-products unit assesses fixed-before-prime-choice degree scheduling; the residue-cut theorem itself is a separate, unreviewed obligation.
The report gives an existential mathematical assessment, not an effective patch-construction implementation or a formal certification of the standard algebraic geometry inputs.
Native Host-invoked independent Reviewer assessment remains required.
